overview.text: Today's key developments span architectural advancements in diffusion models, operational insights into coding agents, automated reasoning approaches, and enterprise partnerships. First, reinforcement learning techniques and unified architectures like Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni are expanding the capabilities of diffusion language models for reasoning and cross-modal tasks. Second, technical investigations into tools like Claude Code reveal backend transparency details regarding background agent transcripts, while analyses highlight evolving inflection points for coding agents in software engineering workflows. Third, automated theorem proving and streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction continue to push the boundaries of research performance. Finally, major lab announcements and enterprise expansions, such as Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Carbon and OpenAI's partnership with ServiceNow, signal continued scaling and integration across the ecosystem. Together, these updates underscore a sustained push toward more capable, unified, and integrated AI systems across research and production environments.

entries.title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
entries.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, enabling bidirectional context modeling and parallel token refinement. Recent studies have applied reinforcement learning (RL) to DLMs and improved their reasoning performance.
entries.why: Improves reasoning performance in diffusion language models by applying reinforcement learning through denoising token credit assignment.

entries.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
entries.summary: Streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE) is essential for latency-sensitive applications. However, current causal systems face two coupled gaps.
entries.why: Addresses coupled gaps in causal streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction systems for latency-sensitive applications.

entries.title: Claude Code regularly sends each background agent’s transcript to its model
entries.why: Reveals operational transparency practices by showing that Claude Code regularly sends background agent transcripts to its model.

entries.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
entries.summary: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and…
entries.why: Explores the bitter lesson in automated theorem proving by contrasting human-designed workflows with scaled agentic reasoning.

entries.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
entries.summary: We propose Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni (NLD-Uni), a unified discrete diffusion large language model (DLLM) for visual understanding and generation tasks. Compared with prior unified diffusion models, NLD-Uni introduces two major innovations.
entries.why: Introduces a unified discrete diffusion large language model for visual understanding and generation via cross-paradigm distillation.

entries.summary: Are concepts and mechanisms unified across modalities in current AI models, or instead implemented separately for each one?
entries.why: Investigates whether concepts and mechanisms are unified or separated across image and text generation modalities.
